#### **Aim :**
To create and manipulate a **list and data frame in R** using tree data, 
extract tree age and circumference, and calculate the **minimum, maximum, 
mean, and standard deviation** of circumference for each tree.

Also, to compare the **average circumference of Tree 3 and Tree 5**.

#### **Theory :**
In R, a **data frame** is a two-dimensional data structure used to store data in rows and columns. A **list** is a flexible data structure that can store different types of objects together.

In this practical, tree data such as **tree number, age, and circumference** are stored and manipulated using lists and data frames. R functions such as `min()`, `max()`, `mean()`, and `sd()` are used to calculate the minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation of tree circumference.

The `split()` function is used to divide the circumference data according to each tree, allowing tree-wise statistical analysis. Finally, the mean circumference of Tree 3 and Tree 5 is compared.

#### **Problem :**
Working with list and data frames in R.
Generate the following data set :

| Tree | S.No. | Age | Circumference |
|------|------:|----:|--------------:|
| 1 | 1 | 118 | 30 |
| 1 | 2 | 484 | 58 |
| 1 | 3 | 664 | 87 |
| 1 | 4 | 1004 | 115 |
| 1 | 5 | 1231 | 120 |
| 1 | 6 | 1372 | 142 |
| 1 | 7 | 1582 | 145 |
| 2 | 8 | 118 | 33 |
| 2 | 9 | 484 | 69 |
| 2 | 10 | 664 | 111 |
| 2 | 11 | 1004 | 156 |
| 2 | 12 | 1231 | 172 |
| 2 | 13 | 1372 | 203 |
| 2 | 14 | 1582 | 203 |
| 3 | 15 | 118 | 30 |
| 3 | 16 | 484 | 51 |
| 3 | 17 | 664 | 75 |
| 3 | 18 | 1004 | 108 |
| 3 | 19 | 1231 | 115 |
| 3 | 20 | 1372 | 139 |
| 3 | 21 | 1582 | 140 |
| 4 | 22 | 118 | 32 |
| 4 | 23 | 484 | 62 |
| 4 | 24 | 664 | 112 |
| 4 | 25 | 1004 | 167 |
| 4 | 26 | 1231 | 179 |

| 4 | 28 | 1582 | 214 |

| 5 | 31 | 664 | 81 |
| 5 | 32 | 1004 | 125 |
| 5 | 33 | 1231 | 142 |
| 5 | 34 | 1372 | 174 |
| 5 | 35 | 1582 | 177 |

**I.** Create a list named tree_data by using the above data set. The list will have three elements viz. Tree number i.e., an ordered factor indicating the measurement is made. The ordering is according to increasing maximum diameter. Tree age i.e., a numeric vector giving the age of the tree (days since 1968/12/31) and Tree circumference i.e., a numeric vector giving tree circumference (mm). This is probably “circumference at breast height”, a standard measurement in forestry.
```{r}
# Tree number
Tree <- factor(rep(1:5, each = 7),
               levels = 1:5,
               ordered = TRUE)
               
# Age of trees
Age <- rep(c(118, 484, 664, 1004, 1231, 1372, 1582), 5)

# Circumference measurements
Circumference <- c(
  30, 58, 87, 115, 120, 142, 145,     # Tree 1
  33, 69, 111, 156, 172, 203, 203,    # Tree 2
  30, 51, 75, 108, 115, 139, 140,     # Tree 3
  32, 62, 112, 167, 179, 209, 214,    # Tree 4
  30, 49, 81, 125, 142, 174, 177      # Tree 5
)

# Create the list
tree_data <- list(
  Tree = Tree,
  Age = Age,
  Circumference = Circumference
)
```
```{r List, echo=FALSE}
cat("The created list is :")
```
```{r}
tree_data
```

**II.** Extract the Tree age and Tree circumference from the list obtained in step 1.
```{r}
tree_age <- tree_data$Age
tree_circumference <- tree_data$Circumference
```
```{r Age, echo=FALSE}
cat("The extracted Age of the tree are :")
```
```{r}
tree_age
```
```{r Circumference, echo=FALSE}
cat("The extracted Circumference of the tree are :")
```
```{r}
tree_circumference
```

**III.** Calculate the tree wise Minimum, Maximum, Mean, and Standard Deviation of Circumference.
```{r}
# Firstly, dividing the circumference measurements according to the tree.
tree_circ <- split(tree_data$Circumference, tree_data$Tree)
```
```{r treewise, echo=FALSE}
cat("The Circumferences of each tree are :")
```
```{r}
tree_circ
```
```{r}
# Calculating tree-wise Minimum, Maximum, Mean and Standard Deviation
tree_min <- sapply(tree_circ, min)
tree_max <- sapply(tree_circ, max)
tree_mean <- sapply(tree_circ, mean)
tree_sd <- sapply(tree_circ, sd)

result <- data.frame(
  Tree = 1:5,
  Minimum = tree_min,
  Maximum = tree_max,
  Mean = tree_mean,
  SD = tree_sd
)
```
```{r result, echo=FALSE}
cat("The calculated Minimum, Maximum, Mean and Standard Deviation tree-wise are :")
```
```{r}
result
```

**IV.** Can we say the average circumference of tree 3 is more than average circumference of tree 5?
```{r}
# Comparing the average circumference of Tree 3 and Tree 5
mean_tree3 <- mean(tree_circ[[3]])
mean_tree5 <- mean(tree_circ[[5]])

cat("Mean circumference of Tree 3:", mean_tree3, "\n")
cat("Mean circumference of Tree 5:", mean_tree5, "\n")

if (mean_tree3 > mean_tree5) {
  cat("Yes, The Average circumference of Tree 3 is more than Tree 5.\n")
} else {
  cat("No, The Average circumference of Tree 3 is NOT more than Tree 5.\n")
}
```

#### **Result :**
The tree data was successfully created and manipulated using **lists and data frames in R**. The minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation of circumference were calculated for each tree.

The average circumference of **Tree 3 was 94 mm**, while that of **Tree 5 was 111.14 mm**. Therefore, **Tree 5 has a higher average circumference than Tree 3**.
